title: Brake Caliper Replacement
summary: Repair guide, labor context, and estimate workflow for brake caliper replacement.
repair_overview: Confirm caliper sticking, leaking, or seized condition
Remove brake hose and caliper assembly
Verify there are no leaks and confirm proper brake operation
tools_required: Brake bleeder bottle or pressure bleeder

torque_specs.label: Wheel lug nuts
torque_specs.value: Vehicle specific - load vehicle for exact spec

torque_specs.label: Caliper bracket bolts
torque_specs.value: Vehicle specific - load vehicle for exact spec

torque_specs.label: Brake hose banjo bolt
torque_specs.value: Vehicle specific - load vehicle for exact spec

repair_steps: Raise and support the vehicle safely.
Confirm caliper and hose connection layout.
Remove caliper hardware and disconnect hose as required.
Install replacement caliper and sealing washers if applicable.
Reconnect brake hose and torque fittings.
Verify there are no fluid leaks.
Reinstall wheel and torque lug nuts.
Confirm brake pedal feel before moving vehicle.
pro_tips: Compare replacement caliper to the original before installation.
Use new sealing washers where required.
Inspect hose condition while the system is apart.
Bleed both sides when needed for balanced brake feel.
warnings: Do not reuse damaged sealing washers.
Do not drive until pedal feel is firm and leaks are ruled out.

diagnostic_context.intro: Caliper replacement often follows brake drag, fluid leaks, or uneven wear discovered during brake inspection.
